endorsements.quote: Therefore, every health degree should include GenAI training, including risks and limits, to prepare students for this integration.

Therefore, we propose the following call to action: increase health literacies (health, media, information, and science) and specifically AI literacy starting as early as preuniversity levels to prepare future generations for the AI-driven health care landscape, as well as offering courses on AI use, risks, biases, and management of AI-generated information in all health degree programs.

unlisted_practices: Provide patients with easy options to opt out of data sharing without facing adverse consequences.
Develop advanced algorithms to detect and flag deep fakes and inaccurate information.
Implement regulations that hold the full chain of dissemination of false information accountable.
Engage technology companies, media, health care professionals, and governments to identify and mitigate the impact of misinformation.
Continuously validate GenAI systems in a transparent manner.
Use inclusive and representative datasets to ensure equitable treatment of all patient groups.
Respect the data sovereignty of communities, including indigenous communities, in AI policies.
Incorporate AI and ethics experts within public health organizations.

Develop international collaboration on AI legislation with global standards, a clear definition of high-risk applications in medicine and public health, and equitable ethical and regulatory guidelines.
Integrate health topics into computer science, ethics, and technology governance education.
Adequately resource public communication, social participation, health promotion, and health education capacities.

screen.reason: This is a viewpoint article offering perspectives and recommendations on generative AI, misinformation, public health practice, policy, and governance.
